8	
9	> Platform: `Adobe Commerce SaaS`
10	
11	## Overview
12	
13	Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service — Adobe's fully managed, versionless
14	edition of Adobe Commerce. Adobe runs and upgrades the commerce
15	backend; projects build the storefront on Edge Delivery Services and
16	extend the platform out-of-process, through APIs, events and App
17	Builder, instead of customizing the application code as on
18	[Adobe Commerce PaaS](adobe-commerce-paas.md). Chosen when a project
19	wants Adobe Commerce without owning upgrades, patches or backend
20	infrastructure.
21	
22	## Stack by layer
23	
24	| Layer | Technology / Tool | Notes |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| Backend/Platform | Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service | Adobe-managed backend with automatic updates; no application code to customize, so no PHP modules or Luma theme |
27	| Backend/Platform | GraphQL supergraph | One endpoint per environment: Storefront Services (Catalog Service, Live Search, Product Recommendations) serve reads; cart, checkout and orders go to the core |
28	| Backend/Platform | REST APIs | Admin and integration APIs — a smaller surface than on PaaS, with the store scope in a request header |
29	| Backend/Platform | Adobe IMS (OAuth) | Required authentication for admin and integration calls; server-to-server credentials for background jobs |
30	| Frontend | Commerce Storefront on EDS | Vanilla JS (ES Modules) block architecture, as on [AEM EDS](aem-eds.md) |
31	| Frontend | Drop-ins (`@dropins/storefront-*`) | Prebuilt commerce components — product page, cart, checkout, account — mounted in blocks |
32	| Frontend | Drop-in SDK (TypeScript / Preact) | Custom drop-ins when the prebuilt ones don't cover a need |
33	| Extensibility | Adobe App Builder (Adobe I/O Runtime) | Serverless actions — the only place for custom backend logic, as on [AEM EDS](aem-eds.md) |
34	| Extensibility | Webhooks | Synchronous calls from Commerce flows to App Builder actions (e.g. validate a cart, price a shipment) |
35	| Extensibility | Adobe I/O Events | Asynchronous Commerce events for App Builder and external systems |
36	| Extensibility | API Mesh | Combines Commerce and third-party APIs into one GraphQL endpoint, as on [Adobe Commerce PaaS](adobe-commerce-paas.md) |
37	| Extensibility | Admin UI SDK | Custom screens and menus in the Commerce Admin |
38	| Extensibility | Integration & Checkout starter kits | Reference App Builder projects for ERP/PIM/CRM integrations and for payment, shipping and tax |
39	| Testing & QA | Jest | Unit tests for custom drop-ins and App Builder actions (`aio app test`) |

> Platform: `Adobe Commerce SaaS`

## Overview

Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service — Adobe's fully managed, versionless
edition of Adobe Commerce. Adobe runs and upgrades the commerce
backend; projects build the storefront on Edge Delivery Services and
extend the platform out-of-process, through APIs, events and App
Builder, instead of customizing the application code as on
[Adobe Commerce PaaS](adobe-commerce-paas.md). Chosen when a project
wants Adobe Commerce without owning upgrades, patches or backend
infrastructure.

## Stack by layer

| Layer | Technology / Tool | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Backend/Platform | Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service | Adobe-managed backend with automatic updates; no application code to customize, so no PHP modules or Luma theme |
| Backend/Platform | GraphQL supergraph | One endpoint per environment: Storefront Services (Catalog Service, Live Search, Product Recommendations) serve reads; cart, checkout and orders go to the core |
| Backend/Platform | REST APIs | Admin and integration APIs — a smaller surface than on PaaS, with the store scope in a request header |
| Backend/Platform | Adobe IMS (OAuth) | Required authentication for admin and integration calls; server-to-server credentials for background jobs |
| Frontend | Commerce Storefront on EDS | Vanilla JS (ES Modules) block architecture, as on [AEM EDS](aem-eds.md) |
| Frontend | Drop-ins (`@dropins/storefront-*`) | Prebuilt commerce components — product page, cart, checkout, account — mounted in blocks |
| Frontend | Drop-in SDK (TypeScript / Preact) | Custom drop-ins when the prebuilt ones don't cover a need |
| Extensibility | Adobe App Builder (Adobe I/O Runtime) | Serverless actions — the only place for custom backend logic, as on [AEM EDS](aem-eds.md) |
| Extensibility | Webhooks | Synchronous calls from Commerce flows to App Builder actions (e.g. validate a cart, price a shipment) |
| Extensibility | Adobe I/O Events | Asynchronous Commerce events for App Builder and external systems |
| Extensibility | API Mesh | Combines Commerce and third-party APIs into one GraphQL endpoint, as on [Adobe Commerce PaaS](adobe-commerce-paas.md) |
| Extensibility | Admin UI SDK | Custom screens and menus in the Commerce Admin |
| Extensibility | Integration & Checkout starter kits | Reference App Builder projects for ERP/PIM/CRM integrations and for payment, shipping and tax |
| Testing & QA | Jest | Unit tests for custom drop-ins and App Builder actions (`aio app test`) |
| Testing & QA | Lighthouse CI | Storefront performance, as on [AEM EDS](aem-eds.md) |

| CI/CD & tooling | `@adobe/aem-cli` | Local storefront dev server |
